newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Chinese boatpeople leave Indonesia for New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Chinese boatpeople leave Indonesia for New Zealand.

text.p: A boat that arrived in Indonesia earlier this week from China carrying 70 men, women and children left the resort island of Lombok on Friday telling authorities they were heading for New Zealand.

"They left at about midday (0500 GMT). They said they were heading for New Zealand," Second Sergeant Sarimukmi, the duty officer at the West Lombok district headquarters in Mataram, told Reuters by telephone.

Sarimukmi said the boat arrived on Thursday carrying the boatpeople from southern China and it moored off the small coastal island of Gili Air, a popular tourist destination off the Lombok coast about 1,000 km (620 miles) east of Jakarta.
He said the passengers appeared to be in good health and after checks by authorities had been allowed to go on their way. He had no further details on the vessel or its occupants.
The official Antara news agency on Friday quoted a local resident as saying the boatpeople had asked for food and medicine as several were ill.
Several children had already died during the journey and were thrown into the sea, the resident said.
Antara quoted the resident as saying there were 200 people.
In recent years hundreds of boatpeople have travelled through the Indonesian archipelago on their way to Australia or New Zealand.
